content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge is grading a multi-verse collision, D5 vs C5, and references C5's own narrowing, so Rule K-C's chain-vs-chain method governs.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' -- read as requiring explicit footing comparison versus merely forbidding the retired stating-verse test; I took the judge's reference to C5's own narrowing and the balanced word-count as chain-level weighing rather than a single-verse contrary test.","why":"The judge text rests on the pressing side's own narrowing and balanced word-count, not on the retired requirement that one verse state the contrary, so it does not breach K-C."}
